correctness.rationale: If t=p−m is coprime to P_m and L_m(t)≤2m, each positive local factor q^(b−1)(q−m) is at most 2m. Therefore every q is at most 3m, each exponent is bounded by e_q, and t divides T_m. When t>B_m this is impossible. For a prime p>m, gcd(p,t)=1; the first iterate is p^(a−1)t and the second is L_m(t) for a=1 or p^(a−2)tL_m(t) for a≥2. A prime q≤m dividing t kills the next iterate and proves strict deficiency. Otherwise t>m and L_m(t)>2m give strict two-iterate abundance: t+L_m(t)>p at a=1, and tL_m(t)>mp for a≥2. Among reduced p modulo P_m, a q dividing m imposes no exclusion and each other q excludes one of q−1 options; CRT and the prime number theorem in fixed progressions therefore give both asserted asymptotics uniformly in the sense of a single finite set of exceptional base primes. At m=4, with t>4 and avoiding 2 and 3, the only t with L_4(t)≤8 are 5,7,11,25,35,55, by enumerating the products of local factors 1,5,3,7 from the permitted prime powers. Only 25 and 55 give primes p≥13. Their chains are 25→5→1 and 55→7→3→0, yielding D_4(29)=31 and D_4(59)=65; at a≥2 their products tL_4(t) are 125>116 and 385>236. Bases 2 and 3 vanish, 5 gives a geometric sum strictly below 5^a, 7 gives 3·7^(a−1), and 11 gives 10 at a=1 and 98·11^(a−2) at a≥2. All remaining p≡1 mod 3 have a vanishing second iterate. Frozen verify.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected; the reported exact finite comparisons were not rerun and are not a substitute for the analytic uniform proof.

evidence: Defant proves for each even m and positive A,η infinitely many p with first-two-iterate surplus exceeding A p^(a−η) for every a≥1, by selecting a CRT class. The indexed theorem instead covers all large classes and both signs, and determines m=2 as well as m=4 exactly.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Defant's published theorem is stronger in surplus for selected bases, not itself the general sign converse. The indexed result is decisive because it covers the same all-class and all-exponent claims; it is not merely the prior existence theorem.

evidence: f611bc4e0ee8 proves L_m(t)≥c_m√t for rough t, with c_m=∏_(m<q≤2m, q prime)(1−m/q), and uses the same first-two-iterate comparison. Its proof explicitly requires t≥m and c_m√t>2m, hence already gives the effective sufficient bound p>m+max(m,(2m/c_m)²). For m=6 this is p>34157.04, whereas the new T_6=49·11·13·17=119119 gives p>119125. Its m=4 proof already handles the full finite boundary. Defant's chosen class at m=4 is 5 mod 6 and alone does not settle the complete finite cases.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new product-divisibility obstruction is a valid elementary alternative for ensuring L_m(p−m)>2m; it does not produce a new classification, a first effective bound, or a demonstrated meaningful quantitative gain. The matched indexed claims are explicit or direct consequences, not guesses from terminology or search scores.
